To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the 2q deletion syndrome is a well-defined and recognisable phenotype; and (ii) the skeletal phenotype is due to hemizygosity of HOXD genes and the facial phenotype due to a critical region encompassing the HOXD cluster and the neighbouring genes.

the 2 q31 deletion syndrome is a well-defined and recognisable clinical entity with a broad spectrum of limb anomalies, and that hemizygosity of the HOXD13 and HOXD genes is the most likely explanation for the observed skeletal defects, whereas the facial dysmorphism is caused by hemizygosity at the 2q21.2 region.

the skeletal phenotype of the 2 q31 microdeletion syndrome, including the SHFM-like phenotype, is a consequence of HOXD haploinsuffi ciency and that the 5’ part of the HOXD cluster and its surrounding regulatory elements are critical for the development of the face in human.

the delineation of a new 2q31 critical region, which includes the DLX genes and their regulatory elements, and the establishment of genotype/phenotype correlations.
the genetic and clinical characterization of patients with interstitial deletions of chromosome 2q.
the delineation of the 2p16.3 and 2q31 microdeletions.

the SHFM5 locus is the HOXD cluster.
a 2q31 microdeletion encompassing the HOXD cluster and the DLX genes causes the observed phenotype.

the skeletal phenotype in 22q13 deletion patients is a consequence of the deletion of the HOXD13 and HOXD12 genes, whereas the facial phenotype is a consequence of hemizygous deletions of the HOXD12 gene and its surrounding regulatory sequences.

the 2 q31.1 microdeltion syndrome is characterised by a variable phenotype that includes limb, heart and ocular anomalies, facial dysmorphism, and intellectual impairment.
the 2 q31 deletion syndrome is a clinically recognisable entity with characteristic features.
the 2p16.3 and 2q31 microdeletions are two different syndromes, with distinct clinical features, and that a critical region for facial gestalt in the 2q microdeletion syndrome can be delineated.

the 2p31.1 microdeltion syndrome is well defined and can be clinically recognisable.
the 2p21.1 and 2q31 microdeletion syndromes should no longer be considered as separate entities.
